reference: Palladium-catalyzed 1,4-Addition of Terminal Alkynes to Conjugated Enones. Organic Syntheses, Vol. 91, pp. 72-82 (2014). DOI: 10.15227/orgsyn.091.0072. URL: https://www.orgsyn.org/demo.aspx?prep=v91p0072
experimental_procedure: In a 100-mL three-necked flask under N2, Pd(OAc)2 and PMe3 (1.0 M in toluene) are stirred 10 min to give a brown solution. Add deionized water (50 mL), then phenylacetylene (0.6 equiv) and ethyl vinyl ketone (1.5 equiv). With vigorous stirring (~1400 rpm), add the remaining phenylacetylene (0.4 equiv) at 0.4 mL/min. Heat at 60 °C for 48 h, then extract with ether, wash with brine, dry (Na2SO4), concentrate, and purify by silica gel column; optional short-path distillation affords the product. [Paraphrased from the source page.]
notes: First step only: Pd(OAc)2/PMe3-catalyzed 1,4-addition of phenylacetylene to ethyl vinyl ketone in water; staged alkyne addition; 60 °C for 48 h.
